content: Never commit Python cache files (__pycache__) or transient DB/test artifacts (test.db-journal, *.db, *.sqlite-journal) to version control — add these patterns to .gitignore and remove any already committed
Never use CORS allow_origins=['*'] in production code — make CORS configuration environment-dependent with specific origins
Make hardcoded business values (ticket prices, cache TTL, rates) and database connection URLs configurable via constants or environment variables instead of embedding them in code
Test public interface methods rather than private methods directly (e.g. avoid testing _validate_venue_data() itself; test the public methods that use it)
Remove unused imports to maintain clean code

Never open, submit, or defer-to-CI a PR with known failing, incomplete, or unverified tests — phrasing like 'tests could not be run/verified in the workspace' or 'let CI decide' is an automatic hard rejection. Tests must be written and confirmed passing locally/in-sandbox before opening the PR. Repeated failure mode (PRs #191, #192, #307).
Use request body with proper schema instead of query parameters for POST endpoints

Validate data integrity constraints at the model level (e.g. prevent negative durations, ensure end_date > start_date) and add business rule validation beyond basic schema validation (duplicate venues, capacity limits, etc.)
Implement comprehensive test coverage for all CRUD operations — include dedicated test classes for POST, PUT, and DELETE endpoints
Use in-memory or shared test databases with proper cleanup instead of separate test database files — separate db files cause test isolation issues
Implement proper format validation for structured data fields — e.g. zip_code regex '^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$' and HttpUrl type for website fields
Whitelist allowed fields for update operations — don't rely on hasattr() checks without validating against dangerous fields like 'id'

Keep PRs strictly scoped to their stated purpose — never bundle unrelated housekeeping changes (e.g. .gitignore edits, config tweaks) into a feature/test PR; split into a separate PR. Recurring issue: PR #307 claimed city-filtering tests and closing issue #306, but the diff only contained an unrelated .gitignore entry — review must verify the diff matches the PR's stated scope/claims before approving.

When a Pydantic schema sets orm_mode/from_attributes = True, use Model.model_validate(result) (or from_orm) to convert ORM/query results instead of manually reconstructing the schema field-by-field — manual construction bypasses the intended conversion mechanism and is flagged in review.

When writing tests for filtering logic (e.g., excluding cancelled items from aggregate counts), add explicit standalone assertions for the exclusion behavior rather than only verifying overall totals, to make test intent clearer to reviewers.

When implementing date-range filtering with same-day boundary semantics, explicitly document in the endpoint docstring whether the boundary date is inclusive or exclusive, to avoid ambiguity for API consumers.

Tests that hardcode a single expected numeric result for an aggregation/computed function (e.g. average=100.0) should include an inline comment deriving that value from the test fixtures, and ideally reference/include unit tests of the underlying calculation logic (e.g. rounding behavior) — so reviewers can verify correctness without tracing into the crud/service implementation.
Always ensure database migration enum values match model definitions exactly — mismatches like migration 'PLANNING' vs model 'planning' cause runtime failures
Use proper foreign key relationships in tests instead of hardcoded IDs (e.g. venue_id=1) — hardcoded values don't test real relationships and fail under real database constraints
Always implement CSRF protection and XSS escaping when using HTMX forms — use Flask-WTF CSRF tokens on data-modifying endpoints (hx-post, hx-delete) and escape user content with {{ content|e }}

Mock chained method calls require explicit return_value assignment at each level — use mock_db.query.return_value.filter.return_value.first.return_value instead of mock_db.query().filter().first.return_value
Never manually manage database sessions by calling next(get_db()) and db.close() — use FastAPI dependency injection or proper session context management
Never mix framework-specific syntax between different frameworks — e.g. using Flask url_for() in FastAPI templates causes incompatibility errors
Use proper SQLAlchemy 2.0 session patterns in tests with contextlib.contextmanager — avoid manual session management with try/except StopIteration handling
Always call database initialization functions or document their usage — e.g. a defined but never-called create_tables() leaves tables uncreated

Registering a SQLAlchemy event listener (e.g. a query counter) on the shared test `engine` imported from tests.conftest causes it to persist globally across all connections/tests instead of scoping to the test under measurement — attach listeners to a per-test connection/session instead, and remove them deterministically (context manager or fixture teardown), not a bare finally block

Confirmed: the merge pipeline does not treat coverage, security, or e2e_tests as blocking quality gates, and review-flagged critical issues also do not block merging — PR #307 was merged despite missing tests, unrelated housekeeping changes, and an explicit unverified-tests disclaimer. Verify and fix CI/review wiring so these gates actually block merges.

Quality gates (feature_pages, e2e_tests, feature_calls, feature_e2e) are unstable/non-deterministic — same-day cycles have shown both 'pass' and 'not_run'/'inconclusive'/'fail' for the same gate; feature_calls has been stuck at 'not_run'. Treat any single-cycle 'pass' or 'not_run' as inconclusive rather than definitive for merge eligibility, and continue monitoring/investigating runner configs for regressions.

Quality gate 'e2e_tests' failing as of 2026-10-06 (14/15 passed) — test_feature_venue_detail_venue_with_no_concerts_returns_empty_list asserts an empty concert list but got a non-empty list containing a 'planned' concert; venue detail endpoint's empty-state filtering logic needs investigation/fix.

Quality gate 'feature_pages' showed status 'not_run' on 2026-10-08 (distinct from pass/fail) — verify the gate is actually being triggered/executed rather than silently skipped before trusting cycle results as fully green.
Never remove essential dependencies that are still in use — pytest, pydantic, alembic, aiosqlite, httpx are needed for testing, schemas, database operations, and FastAPI TestClient imports
Use modern SQLAlchemy 2.0 syntax — DeclarativeBase instead of declarative_base(), .where() instead of .filter() on count() results
Use FastAPI lifespan context manager instead of deprecated @app.on_event('startup') for FastAPI 0.104.1+
Use SQLAlchemy's Enum type for proper database constraints instead of String — storing enum values as strings without db-level enum constraints reduces data integrity
Use Pydantic v2 syntax with `from_attributes = True` and `.model_dump()` instead of deprecated `orm_mode = True` and `.dict()`
Never enable SQL logging in production code — echo=True in the SQLAlchemy engine logs all SQL statements to console and should be configurable via environment variables
Code coverage: 98.1% (confirmed as of 2026-10-11), trending healthy despite not being a blocking quality gate

Never change frameworks without implementing the complete backend infrastructure — e.g. switching from FastAPI to Flask requires implementing all routes, models, and app setup before templates can function
Always implement pagination (limit/offset) on collection GET endpoints — missing pagination causes performance issues with large datasets
Implement foundational layers before dependent components — create models, services, and backend endpoints before writing tests or frontend code that depends on them
Avoid circular imports by placing shared Base classes in a separate module like models/base.py rather than defining them locally

Never open or claim a PR implements a feature, closes an issue, adds/writes tests, or exports schema symbols when the diff doesn't actually contain those changes — verify every new import/exported symbol against included diff hunks, and ensure the PR's 'Changed files' list/diffstat exactly matches every file actually modified, including barrel/index files updated to export new symbols. Repeated failure mode: PR #192 (binary test.db-journal artifact only), PR #257 (100% test additions with no schema/model/endpoint changes), PR #307 (claimed city-filtering backend tests and closing issue #306 but diff only added a .gitignore entry), PR #463 (imported CancelTourRequest/CancelTourResponse from schemas/tour.py and used func.date() in a service file, but the diff omitted src/schemas/tour.py and the func import), PR #486 (claimed to use PriceStatsResponse/get_price_stats but diff only included stats.py/test_stats_api.py, with no actual schema or crud module changes; also left GET /api/v1/stats/prices unregistered as a route). Such mismatched PRs should be rejected/closed, not merged.

Scope database/test-infrastructure changes narrowly. Switching SQLALCHEMY_TEST_DATABASE_URL from a file-based sqlite DB to 'sqlite://' in-memory with StaticPool is a global change affecting every test in the suite and needs explicit review of test isolation/ordering — don't apply such changes globally when only new fixtures need them
Always include referenced template files in PRs when implementing routes — referencing templates without including them breaks the application
API endpoints should return JSON data following REST conventions — returning raw HTML from API endpoints violates standards and complicates testing/maintenance
Integrate validation methods into models via SQLAlchemy's @validates decorator, or remove them — unconnected validation methods are dead code
Implement proper error handling for external dependencies — service methods should handle database connection failures and query timeouts gracefully with appropriate fallback responses
Implement comprehensive test coverage including dedicated unit tests for service layer business logic — endpoint tests alone are insufficient

Date-range filtering with func.date(column) >= func.date(reference) relies on SQLite-specific date() semantics and won't behave identically on other databases (e.g. Postgres) — use database-agnostic date comparisons or cast()/type_coerce for portability.

When implementing cancel/complete endpoints for parent entities with sub-resources (e.g. cancel tour affecting concerts), validate and update the parent entity's own status field too — don't only cascade to children while leaving the parent status unchanged, unguarded against re-cancellation, or unchecked.
Code coverage: 98.1%
Quality gate 'unit_tests' failed on 2026-10-11 yet all 3 PRs still merged — confirms unit_tests is also non-blocking in the merge pipeline, not just coverage/security/e2e_tests.
Quality gate 'feature_calls' showed status 'not_run' on 2026-10-11, alongside feature_pages — both gates are unreliable/non-deterministic and should not be assumed to execute each cycle.
